title: Tesla Opens Its First Tesla Semi Service Centre in Laredo
excerpt: Tesla has opened its first dedicated Tesla Semi Service Centre in Laredo, putting the electric truckmaker's heavy-duty service operation at one of the busiest freight crossings in the country.
content:
Tesla has opened its first dedicated Tesla Semi Service Centre in Laredo, putting the electric truckmaker's heavy-duty service operation at one of the busiest freight crossings in the country.

The company held an opening event at the site on Friday, Nov. 13, featuring Tesla Semi ride-alongs and a tour of the facility, according to Drive Tesla Canada. The centre is at 13505 Regional Drive, just off Interstate 35.

The location is no accident. Laredo's port of entry handles the most land-based trade in the United States, and several key Tesla suppliers sit just across the border in Mexico, including Quanta Computer, Noah Itcech, Brembo and AGP Group.

The Semi is Tesla's electric Class 8 truck, built for freight hauling. A dedicated service centre in Laredo means the trucks running the I-35 corridor — and crossing into Mexico — can be serviced where the freight actually moves, rather than being routed to a general Tesla service location.

Tesla has not said what comes next in Texas, but industry watchers expect a second dedicated Semi centre: the company recently leased a roughly 30,000-square-foot facility in Buda, just south of Austin, though Tesla has not confirmed what it plans to use it for. A service triangle running from Austin to San Antonio to El Paso was publicly discussed in 2025.
